geometry_edits.rationale: A split-wing macro better matches the neighborhood-living brief by keeping one dominant mass while creating a public ground opening at the frontage.
geometry_edits.semantic_role: primary mass re-anchored to allow public threshold

geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the bar-like dominant gesture along the long axis.
Create a visible, usable void instead of a sealed object.
Keep continuity at grade so the opening reads as an entry/public threshold rather than two unrelated fragments.
Align the void to the verified access side to satisfy the active-edge requirement.
Enlarge the carve so it can read as public space and not decorative subtraction.

graph_edits.rationale: Break the single sculpted bar into a more legible split-wing mass so the street edge can open toward a usable ground void instead of remaining sealed.
Keep the dominant gesture oriented as a bar along the long axis while allowing a clearer public opening to form at the frontage.
Introduce an upper connection only after the ground void is established, preserving one dominant mass and avoiding fragmentation.
Encourage a legible ground threshold / entry seam aligned with the access edge.
Reorient the carved void toward the program-frame access side so the frontage becomes public rather than sealed.
Widen the carve so the void reads as an occupiable public cut, not a minor surface nick.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent object in 3D, but its four-view silhouette is dominated by a compact twisted wedge rather than a clear neighborhood bar with an active threshold. The blue access edge is not answered by a legible public void, court, notch, or ground seam; instead the mass stays largely sealed and semantically neutral to the frontage. The form is also too sculptural/top-heavy for the stated compact mixed neighborhood-living brief, and the visible section does not communicate a convincing public ground relationship or calm upper hierarchy. It is not fully fragmented and the geometry is coherent, but program_fit_hard_pass fails because the dominant gesture is not aligned to the required active-edge/public-space logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More civic/cultural than neighborhood-living; the candidate lacks the same legible courtyard/public ground response.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a strong central void and an explicit bridge/threshold condition can support neighborhood-scale public openness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate is much more singular and much less spatially porous; copying this would over-fragment the current bar.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes and a large carved void can create hierarchy while keeping a compact campus-like mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate is too sculpted and top-heavy compared with this calm, access-legible typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple low-rise street-facing pavilion can read as neighborhood-appropriate when the ground edge is open and clearly public.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: this belongs to a larger housing/ramp typology and would push the current brief toward an over-scaled sectional object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced section and inhabited slope can be a valid section strategy for living programs when the roof becomes occupiable.

warnings: Access edge response is weak/opposite: the road frontage is present but not opened with a court, undercut, or entry seam.
The mass is coherent but reads more like a generic sculpted object than a neighborhood living building.
The stepped/tapered silhouette is not the main issue; the issue is that it does not produce usable public void or a clear ground threshold.
No clear section/program logic is visible for living occupancy beyond a compact extruded object.
